summary:
Rondônia stands under the national framework of Brazil. The state has no statute of its own prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity; since 2019 such conduct has been criminalised nationwide on the same footing as racism, and the Rondônia legislature has not enacted a state-level prohibition to supplement it.

In July 2022 Hanier Miranda became the first person in Rondônia to obtain a birth certificate carrying an X sex marker. The civil registry had initially refused the entry for lack of a regulated third-gender procedure, and the marker was secured only after a year-long lawsuit brought by the Center for Legal Practices, Research and Extensions at the Catholic Faculty of Porto Velho.

On 28 August 2025 an ordinance signed by Appellate Judge Daniel Ribeiro Lagos guarantees transgender people the use of their social name and the use of bathrooms and locker rooms in accordance with their gender identity.

Violence against trans people in the state is documented at a measurable level. Twelve murders of transgender people were recorded in Rondônia between 2017 and 2021, and the state was ranked third among those of the North Region for homicide rate; that ranking is regional, and the inventory gives no population denominator behind it. Police recorded 240 reports of violence against LGBTQ people in Rondônia across 2020 and 2021 alone.

School policy has been contested twice at state level. State Law no. 5123, approved in October 2021 and signed on the 19th by Governor Marcos Rocha, banned gender-neutral language in schools; it was suspended by preliminary injunction in November 2021 and struck down on 10 February 2023, so gender-neutral language may be used in Rondônia schools without prohibition or penalty. A further law passed on 10 July 2026 required parental authorisation for classes on gender identity, and a companion measure required it for classes on sexual orientation, sexual diversity and gender equality; the first was enacted by Assembly President Alex Redano after Governor Marcos Rocha neither vetoed nor signed it, and both were struck down on 17 August 2026 by the Court of Justice of Rondônia.
tangentialFactors:
Rondônia was named in 2022 as the worst Brazilian state for public policies concerning the LGBTQ community. The ranking is a national assessment of policy output rather than a measure of incidents per resident, and the inventory provides no scoring methodology or population weighting behind it.

The pattern of the past five years is legislative activity followed by judicial reversal: a gender-neutral language ban enacted in 2021 and struck down in 2023, then two parental-authorisation measures enacted in July 2026 and struck down within a month. A trans visitor can therefore expect proposals of this kind to circulate at state level without knowing in advance whether they are in force.

The state's own enforcement machinery has been found only partly adequate. A civil inquiry preceding the May 2025 recommendations concluded that existing compliance was partial, identifying the absence of specific training courses for firefighters and the lack of a computerised registration and confidentiality system at the state justice department.

Rondônia's third-place position in the North Region homicide ranking and its twelfth documented trans murders over five years sit alongside a national picture that international comparisons distort, since documentation capacity varies sharply between jurisdictions and raw counts track population size.
localsOnly:
On 5 May 2025 the state prosecution service, the federal and labour prosecution services, the federal public defenders' service and the state public defenders' service jointly recommended to Rondônia's social development and justice departments that military police, civil police, firefighters, and penitentiary and socioeducational agents receive regular training on respect for LGBTQIA+ rights. The bodies required a response within 20 business days and a training plan within 60 days, with schedules covering 2025 and subsequent years.

The same recommendation requires gender identity, sexual orientation and social name to be recorded in police occurrence reports and prison records, with data protection and confidentiality safeguards, so that violence against trans women and travestis, including domestic and family aggression, can be monitored. Compliance is supervised by those prosecution and defender bodies.

Residents engaged in the school system are covered by the two 2026 parental-authorisation laws only while those measures are in force; both were struck down by the Court of Justice of Rondônia on 17 August 2026, and no state requirement of parental authorisation for classes on gender identity or sexual orientation stands as a result.

The social name and facilities guarantee of 28 August 2025 is a state-level instrument issued through the judiciary, distinct from the national identity-document rules that govern civil registry entries.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 17 August 2026 ruling of the Court of Justice of Rondônia has been appealed, or whether further parental-authorisation bills are pending before the Rondônia Legislative Assembly, is unresolved in the available material.

The scope of the 28 August 2025 ordinance, in particular whether its social name and bathroom and locker room guarantees extend beyond state judicial and correctional institutions to schools, workplaces and private premises, is unresolved.

Whether civil registries in Rondônia now issue non-binary or X sex markers as routine practice, or whether each application still requires litigation, is unresolved; only the single 2022 case is documented.

The denominator behind the North Region homicide-rate ranking and the methodology behind the 2022 worst-state assessment are not sourced, so neither figure supports a per-capita comparison with other states.

The inventory contains no Rondônia-specific material on health-care access for trans people, custody or detention placement, or entry and border screening. Those layers are carried at national level and are not restated here.
